status: round 3 cut sent: clean-voice audio, full "Feels massive", ~1.5s pause before the spoken address over the end card
concept: A creative presenter talks to camera ABOUT GBX Professional Services (he is an advocate, not the business owner). As he talks he changes backdrop and outfit to show how GBX rebrands a business and its space to fit what it really does, his white tee the same underneath each look. If you do not know what you do best, GBX helps you find it. Closes on gbxps.com.
runtime_plan: Four shots of about 3.5 to 4 s each equal roughly 15 s, then a 2 to 3 s GBX end card. Total about 17 s.
shared_style: Authentic handheld UGC video, 9:16 vertical, shot to look like a phone front camera: natural light, a slight handheld sway, direct address to camera, real and unpolished, shallow phone-camera depth of field. One man throughout, the same person in every shot: bald with a short neat dark beard, thick black-rimmed glasses, a plain white crew-neck t-shirt as his constant base layer under whatever else he wears. Friendly, warm, confident, an Australian everyman in his late thirties. Only the layer over the tee and the room behind him change from shot to shot. No other real brands, no legible logos, words or numbers on anything except the GBX Professional Services mark in shot 1 and on the end card.

voice.direction: One male voice, friendly and down to earth, warm with a light Australian lean, conversational UGC energy like talking to a mate, upbeat and quick but every word clear, no presenter polish, no hard sell.
voice.rule: Describe the voice; never name a real person.
voice.lipsync: Face comes from one character reference image; voice comes from the chosen take. Lip-sync either in OpenArt Seedance element2video (image + audio reference) or in an ElevenLabs flow with a video model, whichever reads more natural on a test clip.
build_options: Preferred: ElevenLabs for the voice (creative connector) for a natural, friendly Australian voice, either picked from creative_list_voices or made with creative_design_voice, then one clean take per line. Higher quality and more controllable than a model-generated voice.
Alternative: let OpenArt Seedance speak natively from a cloned voice reference, as the other GBX social pieces did. Simpler single pipeline, slightly less natural.

build_plan: 1. Generate one hero character image (nano-banana-pro, 9:16) locking bald, beard, black-rimmed glasses, white tee. Approve the face before any video.
2. Generate one short voice sample in the UGC voice, upload it as an audio reference so every clip shares one voice and lip-syncs to it.
3. Generate 4 draft clips (Seedance 2.5 element2video, 9:16, 480p, 4 to 5 s, generateAudio true) with the face image + voice reference, one line each.
4. Stitch with quick UGC transitions (whip and match cut, not slow dissolves), add the end card, optional light bed under the voice.
5. Burn phone-readable captions, verify (frame strip, silencedetect, loudness, yuv420p, audio length), send a 720x1280 review copy.
6. 1080p finals only once the cut is approved.
